newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity rises despite softer cash prices.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity rises despite softer cash prices.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures rose midday Monday in light activity despite steady to softer physical power prices in the western U.S.
"There's a general lack of interest and gas is not doing much," said a Houston futures trader.
Many participants are absent to attend several industry functions around the country this week, market souces said.
As of 1250 EDT, NYMEX June Henry Hub natgas futures were down 0.7 cent at $2.235 per million British thermal units.

Day-ahead firm, peak power prices at the California-Oregon Border (COB) were quoted at $17.00-18.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) compared with Friday's $17.25-18.25. Those at Palo Verde (PV) softened to $24.00-26.00 from $26.00-27.00 Friday.
June COB futures were up 50 cents at $16.60 a MWh, while July COB was up 21 cents at $17.70. Deferred COB months were flat to up nine cents.
June Palo Verde (PV) futures were up 20 cents at $22.30, while June PV climbed six cents to $25.10. Other PV months were mixed.
Cash power prices, especially in the Southwest, were under pressure from more spot power supply, market sources said.
Several generating units including a 750 megawatt (MW) unit at Four Corners and an 875 MW unit at the Intermountain plant returned to service after being shut for repairs or maintenance.
More hydropower from the Northwest could be flowing to the Southwest as early as tomorrow when capacity on the Pacific Intertie is expected to increase.
Late Friday, the board of the Western Systems Coordinating Council announced it endorsed to increase the energy flow on the Pacific Intertie from 6,250 MW to 7,200 MW.

The transmission system, a major conduit in moving cheap hydropower from the Pacific Northwest to southern California, has been running below its maximum capacity of 7,900 MW after two major blackouts in the West last summer.
Bonneville Power Administration said it hopes to begin ramping up capacity on the intertie at midnight.

The western half of the country would generally be warm and dry for the next several days with the exception of the mountainous region in the Southwest where there is chance of scattered thunderstorms.

In the Northwest, temperatures in cities like Portland and Seatttle are expected to hit the mid-70s to mid-80s F. In the Southwest, readings along the coast are projected to run in the 70s-80s, while those in the interior desert area would likely hit the 100s.
